title: Bidirectional LSTM Toxicity Classifier
summary: A CUDA word-level toxicity classifier tokenizes lowercased comments with a regex, truncates to 220 tokens, and builds a training-derived vocabulary retaining terms with frequency at least five, capped at 200,000; other terms map to unknown. It uses learned 300-dimensional embeddings with spatial dropout, two stacked 256-unit bidirectional LSTMs, masked max and mean pooling, two ReLU dense layers with a residual connection, and sigmoid logits for toxicity plus identity auxiliary labels. Training uses length-bucketed shuffled batches. Toxicity binary cross-entropy is sample-weighted to emphasize identity-mention rows and selected toxic/non-toxic subgroup cases, normalized by mean weight; unweighted identity-label BCE is added equally. Adam runs for four epochs with mixed-precision gradient scaling, norm clipping at 1.0, and exponential per-epoch learning-rate decay. Validation inference pads batches, applies a sigmoid to the toxicity logit, and evaluates continuous probabilities.
